dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: kiñcij jñātaṃ dvaitadāyi bāhyālokas tamaḥ punaḥ | viśvādi bhairavaṃ rūpaṃ jñātvānantaprakāśabhṛt ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Waking, with its partial knowing that brings duality; dream, with its outer appearances; and deep sleep, which is darkness: knowing these states, beginning with waking (viśva), as Bhairava's own form, one comes to hold the infinite light.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the three states (viśva or waking, taijasa or dream, prājña or deep sleep) are to be known as expressions of the fourth (turīya), which is Bhairava; in that fourth state duality vanishes and one is filled with the light of infinite consciousness. Wallis and Bäumer read the three phrases in the same way.
dharana.technique_name: Waking, Dream and Deep Sleep as One Light
dharana.instruction: Contemplate waking, dreaming and deep sleep as one awareness passing through three states.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 86 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the one light knowing all three
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is three states in a row (waking, dream, deep sleep) held within one continuous light of awareness.
geometry.svg_hint: three adjacent bands (light, dim, dark) all enclosed in one soft glowing frame
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: One light through three states
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the day's three states are seen as one awareness passing through different conditions. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Hold waking, dream and sleep together in one view
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The three states of waking, dream and deep sleep, contemplated as one awareness
attention.secondary: The light that is present in all three

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Waking, with its partial knowing that brings duality; dream, with its outer appearances; and deep sleep, which is darkness: knowing these states, beginning with waking (viśva), as Bhairava's own form, one comes to hold the infinite light.
adiyogi.method_summary: Recall the waking state you are in now, last night's dreams, and the blankness of deep sleep. Contemplate all three as one awareness passing through different conditions. Rest in that awareness.

honesty.disclosure: Door 063 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 63 (verse 86) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 063 is dharana 63, verse 86. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Purely a contemplation; nothing to change about sleep. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
